sentences.zh: 今年，我对待健康的方式有了很大的不同。

sentences.zh: 过去我总是非常专注于追求极致和做更多的事情。

sentences.zh: 但现在我意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现反而会好得多。

sentences.zh: 我绝非精英运动员，但我确实从中受益匪浅。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很喜欢更深入地了解自己的身体。

sentences.zh: WHOOP 还为我提供了这些可操作的、个性化的见解，让我变得更加有意识，也意味着我每天能做出更明智的决定，

sentences.en: about what I need rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.

sentences.zh: Sam 探索了那些成为我们生命一部分的记忆、痴迷和微小的宝藏。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们要继续剖析 20 多岁的心理学。

sentences.en: So this episode today, it was inspired by an article I saw the other day, essentially commemorating the five years since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 今天这期节目的灵感来源于我前几天看到的一篇文章，它主要是为了纪念新冠疫情爆发五周年。

sentences.en: And the article was basically a series of photos from that time.
sentences.zh: 那篇文章基本上是一系列那个时期的照片。

sentences.en: Pretty fascinating.
sentences.zh: 非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: But what was really, really interesting and what really inspired me so much were people's reactions to this article because it was honestly such a full spectrum
sentences.zh: 但真正让我感兴趣、并给我带来巨大启发的是人们对这篇文章的反应，因为老实说，那是一种全方位的感受，

sentences.en: of grief, confusion, frustration, but specifically a lot of people who were, quite frankly, shocked that it had been so long since COVID had begun because a lot of them reported,
sentences.zh: 包含了悲伤、困惑和沮丧，特别是很多人坦言，他们对疫情已经过去这么久感到震惊，因为他们中的许多人表示，

sentences.en: a lot of them were saying they felt kind of frozen in time at the start of 2020.
sentences.zh: 他们感觉自己仿佛被冻结在了 2020 年初的时间里。

sentences.en: And those five years didn't feel like the typical five years that we would actively experience.
sentences.zh: 那五年感觉并不像我们通常经历的那种五年。

sentences.en: It's this weird sense that, yes, life has moved on.
sentences.zh: 这是一种奇怪的感觉，是的，生活已经继续前行了。

sentences.en: We are no longer in an active pandemic, but it feels like a distinct before and after, before COVID and after COVID.
sentences.zh: 我们不再处于活跃的疫情中，但感觉就像有一个明显的“之前”和“之后”，即新冠疫情前和新冠疫情后。

sentences.en: And a lot of us inevitably missed out on experiences, missed out on opportunities and time because of that chapter.
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人不可避免地错过了那段时期的经历、机会和时间。

sentences.en: And to this day, we still feel like we haven't really caught up or made up for the experiences and milestones we skipped over because of those years.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，我们仍然觉得还没能真正追赶上来，或者弥补那些因那几年而错过的经历和里程碑。

sentences.en: And that reaction, that reaction to the big five years since the pandemic is one I really want to examine today because many, many of my fellow 20-somethings have been in my DMs
sentences.zh: 那种反应，那种对疫情过去五年的反应，是我今天非常想探讨的，因为我的许多 20 多岁的朋友都在私信我，

sentences.en: with questions about this idea of the pandemic skip.
sentences.zh: 询问关于“疫情跳跃”这个概念的问题。

sentences.en: Feeling as if we have missed out on so much and are we ever going to be able to make up for that lost time or will it just forever be a chapter in our lives that we have to grieve?
sentences.zh: 感觉好像错过了太多，我们还能弥补那些失去的时间吗？还是说这注定将永远成为我们生命中必须哀悼的一个篇章？

sentences.en: We in society at large, I think we talk a lot about the long-term consequences of COVID and we talk about it in terms of the loss of precious lives
sentences.zh: 我认为整个社会都在谈论新冠的长期后果，我们谈论的是宝贵生命的逝去，

sentences.en: and the children falling behind in school and the lingering economic impact.
sentences.zh: 以及孩子们学业的落后和挥之不去的经济影响。

sentences.en: All of those are really significant and important, but what we don't consider is the everyday impact of feeling like time has stood still and that we are still behind,
sentences.zh: 所有这些都非常重要且意义重大，但我们没有考虑到那种感觉时间停滞、我们依然落后的日常影响，

sentences.en: especially for people in our 20s because this time is so sacred and we are constantly being told, these are like the best years of your life, like don't waste them,
sentences.zh: 尤其是对于我们 20 多岁的人来说，因为这段时间如此神圣，我们总是被告知：这是你一生中最美好的时光，别浪费它们，

sentences.en: don't blink or they'll be over.
sentences.zh: 别眨眼，否则它们就结束了。

sentences.en: But, you know, that time was taken from us even though it wasn't our choice and we're still trying to adjuSt.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，那段时间被从我们手中夺走了，尽管那并非我们的选择，我们仍在努力适应。

sentences.en: You know, not to sound dramatic, but we did undergo a collective trauma.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不是在危言耸听，但我们确实经历了一场集体创伤。

sentences.en: COVID was a collective trauma and many of us between the ages of 18 to 34 experienced that very differently from other groups and other, I guess, age brackets in the population.
sentences.zh: 新冠是一场集体创伤，我们中 18 到 34 岁的人群对此的体验与人口中其他群体和其他年龄段的人截然不同。

sentences.en: So what are the consequences of that been for our social development, our emotional development, also just our general sense of life satisfaction, but also how do we overcome
sentences.zh: 那么，这对我们的社会发展、情感发展以及我们对生活的一般满意度产生了什么后果？我们又该如何克服

sentences.en: this sense of bitterness, maybe resentment, indignation, sadness over the time, the experiences, the opportunities that we loSt.
sentences.zh: 这种对失去的时间、经历和机会的苦涩、怨恨、愤慨和悲伤呢？

sentences.en: This is really what I want to discuss today.
sentences.zh: 这正是我今天想要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: We can acknowledge the past, we can say this is just awful that this happened, but what next?
sentences.zh: 我们可以承认过去，我们可以说发生这种事真是太糟糕了，但接下来呢？

sentences.en: How do we overcome that?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何克服它？

sentences.en: So without further ado, my lovely, lovely listeners, let's talk about the psychology of the pandemic skip.
sentences.zh: 所以，废话不多说，我亲爱的听众们，让我们来聊聊“疫情跳跃”的心理学。

sentences.en: So the pandemic skip, this concept, it refers to the sense that our mental age is a lot younger than our chronological age because the pandemic has caused us to miss out
sentences.zh: 所谓“疫情跳跃”，这个概念指的是这样一种感觉：我们的心理年龄比实际年龄要小得多，因为疫情导致我们错过了

sentences.en: on very important life experiences that were essential for our development.
sentences.zh: 对我们成长至关重要的重要人生经历。

sentences.en: So essentially, we feel frozen in time and we feel like our development is delayed.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，我们感觉自己被冻结在时间里，感觉我们的发展停滞了。

sentences.en: So you might be 27, but you still feel 23 or 24, which in our 20s is actually quite a huge jump.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经 27 岁了，但感觉自己还是 23 或 24 岁，这在我们 20 多岁的年纪里其实是一个巨大的跨度。

sentences.en: You know, even if in the grand scheme of things, three years is not that large.
sentences.zh: 你知道，即使从宏观角度来看，三年时间并不算太长。

sentences.en: In our 20s, you know, I know people who are now married at 27 who had not even met their partner at 23.
sentences.zh: 但在我们 20 多岁时，我知道有些人 27 岁已经结婚了，而他们在 23 岁时甚至还没见过他们的伴侣。

sentences.en: We can have entirely different jobs, live in entirely different places, have entirely new friends.
sentences.zh: 我们可能从事着完全不同的工作，住在完全不同的地方，拥有全新的朋友。

sentences.en: I really do believe that a year in our 20s is five years any other time.
sentences.zh: 我真的相信，20 多岁时的一年相当于其他时期的五年。

sentences.en: And that really goes to show, I just think, how much could change and maybe should have changed during that period of the pandemic where we were in lockdown, we couldn't travel.
sentences.zh: 这真的说明了，我认为，在疫情期间我们处于封锁状态、无法旅行时，有多少事情可能改变，或者本应该改变，

sentences.en: or just we were experiencing a global emergency.
sentences.zh: 或者仅仅是因为我们正在经历一场全球紧急状况。

sentences.en: So pandemic skip, pandemic pause, it's all the same thing.
sentences.zh: 所以“疫情跳跃”、“疫情暂停”，其实都是一回事。

sentences.en: Essentially, there was this isolation and almost break from reality caused by COVID that has resulted in a lot of long-term developmental shifts and also grief.
sentences.zh: 本质上，新冠导致了一种隔离，甚至是一种与现实的断裂，这导致了许多长期的发展转变，也带来了悲伤。

sentences.en: Grief for many of us.
sentences.zh: 对我们许多人来说，是悲伤。

sentences.en: So why does this happen?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么会发生这种情况呢？

sentences.en: Why do we feel frozen in time?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会感觉被冻结在时间里？

sentences.en: What's the long-term reaction to this?
sentences.zh: 对此的长期反应是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I have three psychological explanations for why you feel like you cannot move on from these years and you feel like you cannot move on from the lost time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对于为什么你觉得无法从这些年走出来，以及觉得无法从失去的时间中走出来，我有三个心理学解释。

sentences.en: The first is that traumatic experiences tend to give us a warped sense of time.
sentences.zh: 第一点是，创伤性经历往往会给我们一种扭曲的时间感。

sentences.en: Now, the COVID pandemic and the ensuing lockdowns, that wasn't just
sentences.zh: 现在，新冠疫情以及随后的封锁，那不仅仅是

sentences.en: 30 seconds of trauma.
sentences.zh: 30 秒的创伤。

sentences.en: That wasn't even a few days of trauma or even a few months.
sentences.zh: 那甚至不是几天的创伤，也不是几个月的创伤。

sentences.en: It was for some people years, years of going through something where every single day you had no idea what was happening, case numbers were rising, you had no idea, you know,
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，那是几年，几年里你每天都不知道发生了什么，病例数在上升，你根本不知道，你知道，

sentences.en: what the government was going to say you needed to do, if toilet paper was going to run out, you know, if you would be able to see your friends.
sentences.zh: 政府会说你需要做什么，卫生纸会不会用完，你知道，你是否还能见到你的朋友。

sentences.en: That is traumatic because it is so deeply uncertain and threatens our core sense of security.
sentences.zh: 那是创伤性的，因为它充满了极度的不确定性，威胁到了我们核心的安全感。

sentences.en: There was one study done during that time that surveyed thousands of Americans in the first six months of the pandemic and they found that for a lot of them time felt like
sentences.zh: 在那个时期进行的一项研究调查了疫情前六个月的数千名美国人，他们发现对很多人来说，时间感觉

sentences.en: it had either sped up or slowed down.
sentences.zh: 要么加速了，要么减慢了。

sentences.en: This cognitive reaction, this warped sense of time is actually quite common after some kind of unprecedented collective trauma like a natural disaster or a global pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这种认知反应，这种扭曲的时间感，在经历过自然灾害或全球大流行等某种前所未有的集体创伤后，其实相当普遍。

sentences.en: So the pandemic also had the effect of really stripping away external markers of time.
sentences.zh: 所以疫情还有一个效果，就是真正剥夺了时间的外部标记。

sentences.en: So things like birthday celebrations, you know, a lot of them took place over Zoom that didn't feel as important.
sentences.zh: 比如生日庆祝活动，你知道，很多都是通过 Zoom 进行的，感觉没那么重要。

sentences.en: Job transitions, life transitions, like moving from graduate into your first full-time job, commutes, social events, all things that would give us a sense that time was passing,
sentences.zh: 工作变动、人生转折，比如从毕业生转入第一份全职工作、通勤、社交活动，所有这些能让我们感觉到时间在流逝的事情，

sentences.en: they disappeared and that has led to what some psychologists will now call the Groundhog Day effect.
sentences.zh: 它们都消失了，这导致了现在一些心理学家所称的“土拨鼠日效应”。

sentences.en: Groundhog Day after the very famous movie with Bill Murray where his day just feels like it's repeating and repeating and repeating, something that I think a lot of us experience
sentences.zh: “土拨鼠日”源自比尔·默瑞主演的那部非常著名的电影，他在电影里的一天感觉在不断地重复，这我认为是我们许多人

sentences.en: during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 在疫情期间所经历的。

sentences.en: So without the usual kind of milestones to differentiate days, weeks and months, time became a blur and many people if they're asked to recall an event and I say did that happen
sentences.zh: 所以，没有了通常用来区分日子、周和月的里程碑，时间变得模糊不清，许多人如果被要求回忆一件事情，我问那是发生在

sentences.en: 2021 or 2022, they don't know.
sentences.zh: 2021 年还是 2022 年，他们根本不知道。

sentences.en: It's just one big lump of years to us with no events, situations, ways to distinguish.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，那只是一大块没有事件、没有情境、没有区分方式的岁月。

sentences.en: There was also this interesting interaction some researchers are pointing to in our age group of people experiencing accelerated aging but stunted growth.
sentences.zh: 还有一些研究人员指出的在我们这个年龄段中，人们经历着“加速衰老但成长停滞”的有趣互动。

sentences.en: So a lot of us might feel like we actually aged faster during the pandemic because of stress and uncertainty, having to skip important milestones and just enter the next chapter
sentences.zh: 所以我们很多人可能觉得在疫情期间因为压力和不确定性，实际上衰老得更快了，不得不跳过重要的里程碑，毫无准备地进入下一个篇章。

sentences.en: unprepared.
sentences.zh: 这导致了，你知道，一种我们衰老得更快的错觉，但另一方面，我们也觉得自己的个人成长停滞了。

sentences.en: That's leading to, you know, a sense that we've aged faster but then on the other side we also feel like we have paused our personal growth.
sentences.zh: 所以我们回到了和父母同住的状态，我们被困在停滞的工作、停滞的关系中，因为我们无处可去，这种双重性创造了一种令人不安的

sentences.en: So we are back to living with our parents we were stuck in stagnant jobs, stagnant relationships because we had nowhere else to go and that duality has created an unsettling
sentences.zh: 体验，即在人生的现阶段既太年轻又太老。

sentences.en: experience of being both too young and too old for where you are in life.
sentences.zh: 你觉得哦，你知道，

sentences.en: You feel like oh, you know,
sentences.zh: 我太老了，不能整天出去聚会，但同时我又觉得足够年轻，可以做那些事情，因为我之前错过了。

sentences.en: I'm too old to be going out partying all the time but also I still feel young enough to be doing those things because I missed out previously.
sentences.zh: 所以还有一个术语叫“发育停滞”，不是指

sentences.en: So there's another term for this it's called arrested development not the
sentences.zh: 那部电视剧，尽管那是一部精彩的

sentences.en: TV show although what a brilliant
sentences.zh: 电视剧，但这个术语真正指的是那些心理上被困在比实际年龄更年轻的情感阶段的年轻人，即 20 多岁的人，他们

sentences.en: TV show but the term really refers to young adults people in their 20s who are mentally stuck at a younger emotional age than their chronological age and are not developing
sentences.zh: 没有以预期的速度在心理上发展，通常是因为创伤或某种非常强烈的压力源。

sentences.en: mentally at the expected rate because of normally it's trauma or some kind of really intense stressor.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，那个压力源、那个创伤就是疫情，所以像你我这样的年轻人内部存在着一种成长停滞，也许社会并没有广泛意识到，但我们

sentences.en: in this case that stressor that trauma was the pandemic and so there is a stunted growth within young adults like you and me that maybe society doesn't recognize at large but we
sentences.zh: 绝对能感觉到。

sentences.en: definitely feel.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么“疫情跳跃”的第二个心理学原因是：疫情夺走了我们的自主感，让我们感到无能为力，而我们至今还没找回这种感觉。

sentences.en: Okay, so the second psychological reason for the pandemic skip the pandemic took away our sense of agency and it made us feel powerless we haven't gotten that back yet.
sentences.zh: 这对 20 多岁的人来说非常重要，拥有自主感，感觉你可以掌控自己的人生，在这段时间的发展中是非常非常重要的。

sentences.en: Now this matters a lot for people in their 20s having a sense of agency feeling like you can direct your own life is really really important to develop during this time.
sentences.zh: 我们人生的这个阶段，确实是我们锻炼独立肌肉、锻炼自主肌肉的时期，这体现在一些非常重大的时刻，比如搬出

sentences.en: This period of our life is really the period where we flex that independence muscle, we flex that agency muscle and that is represented by really big moments like moving out of
sentences.zh: 家、独自旅行、赚取自己的钱、自由恋爱。

sentences.en: home, solo traveling, earning your own money, dating freely.
sentences.zh: 疫情限制了所有这些活动，限制了我们所有的选择，让我们更加依赖父母，而且我们还，你知道，由于封锁
